tools.name: list_domains
tools.description: List every sending domain on the KingSMTP account. Returns for each domain its name, whether it is verified, and the status of its SPF, DKIM, return path and MX records. Use this first to see which domains exist before calling get_domain, verify_domain, delete_domain, send_email or add_route. Read-o

tools.name: add_domain
tools.description: Add a new sending domain to the account. Returns the exact DNS records (ownership TXT, SPF, DKIM, return path) that must be created at the domain registrar before the domain can send. The domain is not usable until those records exist and verify_domain succeeds. Fails if the domain already exists or

tools.name: get_domain
tools.description: Get one domain on the account with its verification status and the exact DNS records (type, name, value) that must exist at the registrar (including the ownership TXT record while unverified). Use this to tell the user which records to add or fix. Read-only.

tools.name: verify_domain
tools.description: Re-check the DNS records of a domain now and mark it verified when all required records are found. Returns the updated domain status. Call this after the user has added the records from add_domain or get_domain; DNS changes can take minutes to hours to propagate, so a failed check can be retried lat

tools.name: delete_domain
tools.description: Permanently remove a domain from the account. After deletion no email can be sent from that domain and its inbound routes stop working; to use it again it must be added and verified again. Ask the user to confirm before calling.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: Show the account plan, plan expiry date, the current billing period, emails used and remaining in that period (including extra top-up emails), delivery counts for the period and the number of domains used versus the plan limit. Use this before large sends or to answer "how many emails do I have left

tools.name: get_stats
tools.description: Daily sending statistics for the last N days: per day the number of emails sent, delivered, bounced, blocked, held and received, plus totals for the whole range. Use get_usage for the current billing period instead. Read-only.

tools.name: list_messages
tools.description: List recent sent (outgoing) and received (incoming) emails, newest first. Each item has id, direction, from, to, subject, delivery status (for example Sent, Bounced, HardFail, Held) and time in UTC, with pagination totals. To look up one specific email, use "search" with the recipient address or par

tools.name: list_suppressions
tools.description: List the addresses on the suppression list: email is never sent to these addresses. Each item shows the address, the reason it was added (for example a bounce or an unsubscribe), when it was added and when it expires (null = never). Use check_suppression to test a single address. Read-only.

tools.name: check_suppression
tools.description: Check whether one email address is on the suppression list and, if so, why and until when. Returns not found if the address is not suppressed. Use this when an email to a specific address is not being delivered. Read-only.

tools.name: add_suppression
tools.description: Add an email address to the suppression list so no email is sent to it, for example when a user asks to never receive email again. Returns the stored entry. Adding an address that is already suppressed is harmless. Removing an address is only possible by the account owner in the KingSMTP dashboard,

tools.name: list_webhooks
tools.description: List the webhooks on the account (id, URL, enabled, subscribed events) and the full list of available event names, such as MessageSent, MessageDelayed, MessageDeliveryFailed, MessageBounced and MessageHeld. Paid plans only. Read-only.

tools.name: get_webhook
tools.description: Get one webhook by id: its URL, whether it is enabled and which events it receives. Paid plans only. Read-only.

tools.name: add_webhook
tools.description: Create a webhook: KingSMTP will POST a JSON event to this https URL whenever one of the chosen delivery events happens. Give either "events" (names from list_webhooks) or all_events=true. Returns the new webhook with its id. Paid plans only.

tools.name: set_webhook_enabled
tools.description: Turn an existing webhook on or off without deleting it. Returns the updated webhook. Safe to repeat. Paid plans only.

tools.name: test_webhook
tools.description: Send one test event to the webhook URL now and report whether it was delivered (delivered true/false and the HTTP status code returned by the URL). Use this to check that the receiving endpoint works. Limited to a few tests per hour. Paid plans only.

tools.name: delete_webhook
tools.description: Permanently delete a webhook; its URL stops receiving events. To pause instead, use set_webhook_enabled. Ask the user to confirm before calling. Paid plans only.

tools.name: list_routes
tools.description: List the inbound routes: incoming email for an address on one of the account domains (or * for the whole domain) and where it is forwarded to (an email address, an https URL or an SMTP server). Paid plans only. Read-only.

tools.name: get_route
tools.description: Get one inbound route by id: the receiving address and where its email is forwarded to. Paid plans only. Read-only.

tools.name: add_route
tools.description: Forward incoming email for an address on a verified domain of the account to an email address, an https URL (the email is POSTed as JSON) or an SMTP server (smtp://host:port). The domain MX record must point to KingSMTP for email to arrive (see get_domain). Returns the new route with its id. Paid pl

tools.name: delete_route
tools.description: Permanently delete an inbound route; email to that address is no longer forwarded. Ask the user to confirm before calling. Paid plans only.

tools.name: send_email
tools.description: Send one transactional email (for example an order confirmation, password reset or test email) from a verified domain on the account. findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "send_email" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

evidence.snippet: send_email

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_usage, get_stats, list_messages, list_suppressions, check_suppression, add_suppression, list_webhooks, get_webhook, test_webhook, list_routes, get_route · Private data: list_domains, add_domain, get_domain, verify_domain, add_route, send_email · Public sink: add_domain, delete_domain, list_messages, list_suppressions, check_suppression, add_suppression, get_webhook, add_webhook, set_webhook_enabled, test_webhook, delete_webhook, list_routes, get_route, add_route, delete_route, send_email · Destructive: delete_domain, delete_webhook, delete_route, send_email.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_usage, get_stats, list_messages, list_suppressions, check_suppression, add_suppression, list_webhooks, get_webhook, test_webhook, list_routes, get_route · Private data: list_domains, add_domain, get_domain, verify_domain, add_route, send_email · Public sink: add_domain, delete_domain, list_messages, list_suppressions, check_suppression, add_suppression, get_webhook, add_webhook, set_webhook_enabled, test_webhook, delete_webhook, list_routes, get_route, add_route, delete_route, send_email · Destructive: delete_domain, delete_webhook, delete_route, send_email

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
